providers.title: Pretree
providers.scope: A set with a ternary betweenness relation satisfying four axioms that hold for the vertices of a tree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Four points in a row
providers.scope: Three implications that place four points of a pretree in a row.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals along a chain
providers.scope: The interval between the ends of a finite sequence of points lies in the union of the intervals between consecutive points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite pretrees and finite trees
providers.scope: Every finite pretree is a set of vertices of a finite tree with the betweenness of the tree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cycles of adjacent points
providers.scope: Distinct points of a pretree that are cyclically adjacent are pairwise adjacent.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Directions
providers.scope: A linear subset of a pretree with two chosen points has exactly one direction in which the first precedes the second.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals are ordered
providers.scope: A closed interval of a pretree is an arc, ordered from one end to the other, and its ends are determined by it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniqueness of medians
providers.scope: Three points of a pretree have at most one median.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Half-open intervals
providers.scope: In a dense pretree, two half-open intervals with the same closed end that are equal have the same open end.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Complete and dense does not imply median
providers.scope: A tripod with a half-open segment next to the centre removed on one leg is a complete dense pretree in which three points have no median and an interval has a cut that is not made at a point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ends of half-open intervals
providers.scope: In a dense median pretree, if the half-open interval from x to y lies in the closed interval from x to z, then y lies in it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cuts are made at points
providers.scope: In a complete dense median pretree, every partition of a closed interval into two arcs is made at a point of the interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals have no gaps
providers.scope: In a complete dense median pretree every nonempty subset of a closed interval has a least upper bound in the interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gates
providers.scope: In a tree, the path from a vertex to a point of a given path passes through the gate of the vertex, and the path between two vertices with different gates runs through both gates.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From weakly to strongly dense
providers.scope: In a median pretree the medians of triples from a weakly dense set form a strongly dense set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cantor's theorem
providers.scope: Any two nonempty countable dense totally ordered sets without ends are order isomorphic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order type of intervals
providers.scope: In a complete separable median pretree every interval with distinct ends is order isomorphic to the real interval [0,1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals are arcs
providers.scope: Under the assumptions of the theorem, every interval of the pretree with distinct ends is homeomorphic to the real interval [0,1], by an order isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Small intervals
providers.scope: Every neighbourhood of a point contains the intervals from that point to all points of a smaller neighbourhood.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Countable base
providers.scope: The sets H(p,q) with p, q in a countable strongly dense set form a subbase of the topology, so the space is metrizable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dendrites from pretrees
providers.scope: A compact space with a countable dense subset carrying a complete dense median pretree structure with open sets H(x,y) is a dendrite, and the pretree intervals are its only arcs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flows towards points
providers.scope: A flow is the flow towards a point a exactly when it flows from every other point to a.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adding a point for a flow
providers.scope: For a flow on a pretree, adding one terminal point whose betweenness is given by the flow yields a pretree in which the flow is the trace of the flow towards the new point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The pretree of a pretree and its flows
providers.scope: A pretree together with the set of all its flows is a pretree in which every flow is terminal and is the trace of the flow towards itself.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cofinal arcs
providers.scope: Directed arcs with a common final segment on which their orders agree have the same flow.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The flow of a directed arc
providers.scope: The relation defined by a directed arc is a flow; on the arc it is the order, and from a point of the arc it reaches exactly the later points of the arc.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Arcs with the same flow
providers.scope: Two directed arcs with a common point and the same flow are cofinal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Restriction to a full subset
providers.scope: If the part of a directed arc inside a full subset is endless, the flow of the arc restricts on the subset to the flow of that part.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Completeness and suprema
providers.scope: A pretree is complete if and only if every directed arc has a supremum.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals between flows
providers.scope: Two different flows have a point of the pretree between them; the interval between the flows towards two points is the closed interval between the points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Betweenness of flows
providers.scope: A flow r lies between flows p and q if r is the flow towards a point between p and q, or r is not a flow towards a point and no point lies both between p and r and between r and q.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The flows form a pretree
providers.scope: The set of flows of a pretree with this betweenness is a pretree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Medians of flows
providers.scope: Every three flows have a median; when no point and none of the three flows serves, it is the flow that goes where two of the three go.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Completeness
providers.scope: Every arc in the pretree of flows is an interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The completion
providers.scope: Every pretree embeds, with its betweenness, in the complete median pretree of its flows.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Star
providers.scope: A set of at least two points of a pretree that is full and is maximal among the sets with no betweenness relation among their points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The flow of a star
providers.scope: From each point the flow of a star runs along the interval to the nearest point of the star; this is a flow, and the star is the set of points from which it runs nowhere.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Classes and type of a flow
providers.scope: The arcs along which a flow runs fall into classes, each endless or ending in one point; the type of the flow counts the classes of each kind.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Three kinds of flows
providers.scope: Every flow on a nonempty pretree is exactly one of: the flow towards a point, the flow of a star, the flow of an endless directed arc; the type decides which.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Points of the pretree are not adjacent
providers.scope: Between the flows towards two different points of a pretree there is always a further flow in the completion.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adjacent points of the completion
providers.scope: Two points of the completion are adjacent exactly when one is the flow towards a point a and the other is a different flow that runs nowhere from a; so exactly one of them is a point of the pretree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Neighbours and finite intervals
providers.scope: A flow of type (m,n) that is not a flow towards a point has n neighbours; a finite interval of the completion alternates between points of the pretree and other flows.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Neighbours and branches
providers.scope: The neighbours in the completion of a point a of the pretree correspond one to one to the branches at a, the classes of the relation that a is not between two points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite intervals are chains
providers.scope: A finite interval of a pretree is a chain of points, each adjacent to the next, in the order of the interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Discrete median pretrees and trees
providers.scope: A pretree with finite intervals in which every three points have a median is the vertex set of exactly one tree; its edges join the adjacent pairs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Discrete pretrees in trees
providers.scope: Every pretree with finite intervals is a set of vertices of a tree, with the betweenness of the tree, in which each further vertex is joined to at least three points of the pretree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Completion of a finite pretree
providers.scope: The completion of a finite pretree is the vertex set of a finite tree in which every edge joins a point of the pretree to a flow that is not a flow towards a point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quotient pretree
providers.scope: For an equivalence relation with full classes on a pretree, the set of classes is a pretree: a class lies between two others if one of its points lies between them.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals map onto intervals
providers.scope: The quotient map sends the interval between two points onto the interval between their classes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A quotient of a quotient
providers.scope: A full relation on a quotient pulls back to a full relation on the pretree, with the same quotient.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quotients of median pretrees
providers.scope: A quotient of a median pretree by a full relation is median, and the quotient map preserves medians.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quotients of complete pretrees
providers.scope: A quotient of a complete pretree by a full relation is complete.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The least codense relation
providers.scope: Among the full relations on a pretree whose quotient is dense there is a least one; its quotient is the dense quotient.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rational subsets
providers.scope: Two points are identified in the dense quotient exactly when the interval between them contains no countable linear subset that is densely ordered without ends.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The derived relation
providers.scope: Identifying points whose classes are joined by a finite interval gives a coarser full relation, equal to the given one exactly when its quotient is dense.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reaching the least codense relation
providers.scope: Starting from equality and repeating the derived relation along the ordinals, with unions at limits, one reaches the least codense relation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rational subsets in the completion
providers.scope: Two points of the completion are identified in its dense quotient exactly when no rational subset consisting of points of the pretree lies between them.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The dense quotient of the completion
providers.scope: The dense quotient of the completion of a pretree is a complete dense median pretree, and it contains the dense quotient of the pretree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two cut points
providers.scope: Two different cut points of a connected Hausdorff space split it into three nonempty open sets and the two points, arranged in a row.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The pretree of a connected space
providers.scope: A connected Hausdorff space is a pretree when a point lies between two others if it has a separation with one of them on each side; the points between others are the cut points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Branches meet connected sets in connected sets
providers.scope: A closed set with at least two points and one boundary point meets every closed connected set in a connected set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intersections of compact connected sets
providers.scope: In a Hausdorff space, the intersection of a family of compact connected sets that is closed under finite intersections is connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intersections of branches
providers.scope: Every intersection of branches of a connected Hausdorff space meets each compact connected set in a connected set; in a compact space it is connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The map to the completion and betweenness
providers.scope: For a pretree M with a subset T, the map that sends a point of M to the flow of T towards it sends points of T between two points to points between the images, and conversely.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Images of the points on the side of a flow
providers.scope: A point of M that lies, for every point a of T, on the side of a on which a flow p lies is mapped to p or to a neighbour of p in the completion.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The completion of a set of cut points
providers.scope: For a compact connected Hausdorff space and a set T of cut points, every point of the completion of T is the image of a point of the space or adjacent to the image of a point of T; the set of points on the side of a flow is nonempty, closed and connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fibres of the quotient map
providers.scope: Two points of a compact connected Hausdorff space have the same image in the quotient exactly when no rational subset of the chosen cut points lies between them.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Preimages of preclosed sets
providers.scope: The preimage in the space of a preclosed subset of the completion of the set of cut points is closed and connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quotient is a continuum
providers.scope: The quotient is a compact connected Hausdorff space, and the preimage of every closed connected subset is closed and connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The dendrite quotient
providers.scope: If the space has a countable dense subset, the quotient is a dendrite; its pretree intervals are its arcs, and its pretree is the pretree of its topology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spaces in which points are separated by points
providers.scope: A compact connected Hausdorff space with a countable dense subset in which any two points are separated by a third point is a dendrite.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
